differences.title: 1. CONNECTION ESTABLISHMENT
differences.leftDesc: QUIC uses TLS 1.3 for faster connection setup, often achieving 0-RTT for subsequent connections, minimizing latency and improving perceived performance significantly.
differences.rightDesc: TCP requires a three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) before data transfer, adding round-trip time. Subsequent connections reset this process.

differences.title: 2. HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCKING
differences.leftDesc: QUIC streams are independent. Packet loss on one stream doesn't block others, dramatically improving performance for multiplexed traffic like HTTP/3.
differences.rightDesc: TCP suffers from head-of-line blocking. A lost packet on any stream (in a single TCP connection) stalls all subsequent data.

differences.title: 3. TRANSPORT LAYER
differences.leftDesc: QUIC runs over UDP, allowing it to bypass operating system kernel limitations and implement advanced features like congestion control in user space.
differences.rightDesc: TCP is tightly integrated into the OS kernel. Modifying or updating its behavior requires kernel patches, making evolution slow and complex.

differences.title: 4. PACKET LOSS RECOVERY
differences.leftDesc: QUIC packets contain acknowledgments for individual streams, enabling more precise loss detection and faster retransmission, even with packet reordering.
differences.rightDesc: TCP uses sequence numbers for ACKs. It's harder to pinpoint specific lost packets, especially with out-of-order delivery.

differences.title: 5. CONNECTION MIGRATION
differences.leftDesc: QUIC connections are identified by a Connection ID, allowing them to survive network changes like switching from Wi-Fi to cellular without interruption.
differences.rightDesc: TCP connections are bound to IP addresses and ports. A change in network means the connection breaks and must be re-established.

differences.title: 6. ENCRYPTION
differences.leftDesc: QUIC encrypts almost all data, including handshake packets, by default using TLS 1.3. This enhances security and privacy from the start.
differences.rightDesc: TCP encryption (TLS/SSL) is applied as a separate layer. The initial handshake is unencrypted, potentially exposing metadata.

differences.title: 7. CONGESTION CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: QUIC's congestion control is implemented in user space, allowing for rapid experimentation and deployment of advanced algorithms like BBR without kernel changes.
differences.rightDesc: TCP congestion control is typically managed by the operating system kernel. Deploying new algorithms requires kernel updates, which is slow.
